A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have visualized the conformational change of a CNG channel in lipid bilayer and found that the CNBD undergoes dramatic conformational change during the interconversion of different ligand binding states.
the CNBD movements may be converted to the pore opening by the C-linkers in a iris diaphragm like mechanism.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the cyclic nucleotide binding domains (CNBDs) undergo dramatic conformation changes during the inter-conversion between the resting (apocGMP) and activated (cAMP bound) states: the domains approach the membrane and spread away from the 2-fold channel axis accompanied with a clockwise rotation with regard to the pore domains.
the conformational change of the CNBD is transmitted to the pore domain by the C-linkers to open the channel in an iris diapragm-like manner.
